summary: Minimal installation runs the Nex wizard in a text frontend and writes the same handoff, so both installer modes install the same host. API impact: none.

guide.reason: Minimal installation no longer asks Debian's language, networking, partitioning and GRUB questions; it asks the wizard's questions, enforces the same password and disk rules, and now creates the management bridge. The documented steps, expected result and troubleshooting had to change with it.

api.reason: Installer frontend only. No Controller/Core route, agent command, event or stream is added or changed; the wizard handoff is a private file read by nex-config inside the same initrd, which is unchanged.

roadmap.reason: No published roadmap milestone changes: this brings an existing installer mode up to the behaviour the guide already described. The decision, rejected alternatives and held-back scope are recorded in docs/plans/2026-09-21-minimal-install-parity.md.

state.reason: Installation-time configuration of the host being built. No durable Controller or pool-scoped record is created, read or changed; the installed host's own /etc files and its Core records remain the authority, exactly as with a graphical installation.

verification.method: Established from the pinned Debian 13 installer images that install.amd/gtk/initrd.gz carries newt.so and text.so and that S62Xorg starts Xorg only for the gtk frontend, and that install.amd/initrd.gz carries no glib, which is why minimal now boots the Nex initrd with DEBIAN_FRONTEND=newt rather than bundling libraries. bash installer/check.sh, the seven existing installer regressions and the new tests/integration/installer-text-wizard.py all pass on 2026-09-21. The new check drives the wizard against a fixture machine under NEX_WIZARD_ROOT and asserts the question order, Go Back over a skipped step, that only the supported disk is offered (not the undersized, removable, read-only, partition or installation-media devices), that the erase confirmation names the disk and resets, and the exact handoff written; the handoff is then decoded with GKeyFile the way nex-config reads it, confirming the password, DNS, VLAN and disk size round-trip. Three mutations (skipping the UTC zone step, accepting removable disks, dropping the password escaping) were each caught. No ISO was built and no installation was performed: a booted minimal installation and a comparison of the installed br0, nexN names, VLAN and DNS against a graphical installation remain outstanding, and the serial entry still runs Debian's own questions.
